title: Corgi Town - completely AI generated - free on Itch
author: jbradleybush
selftext:
Ok, I have been building up my AI coding for the last few years now (was once a pretty good coder as I started in assembly, fortran, pascal, lisp, etc.). I understand product design and play a lot of games now and through the years (including with my kids). 

I designed Corgi Town ([https://jbradleybush.itch.io/corgi-town](https://jbradleybush.itch.io/corgi-town)) after I used Meshy to build a corgi that looked like my dog Pippy and though I wonder if I could make a "real" game. I had made one other pretty cool remake of the 1980's game Archon and I had made a few other playable "demos".  

The first thing I did is build all the spec of what I wanted the game to do and then art direction with ChatGPT which I iterated through quite a bit for character, item, level designs. 

THen I got chatgpt to break out all the 2D views of the 3d objects and had claude load each of these through Meshy to create optimized 3D items and had Claude code write the code and use blender to do some of the assembly, normalization and animations. I used some scripts created by Create with Mark and learned a ton from him about how to go about this. It is a $9 package here ([https://www.createwithmark.co/bundle/](https://www.createwithmark.co/bundle/)) disclaimer: this is not an ad. I don't know Mark. I am just a guy that likes to make things. 

I created my own scoring system against my original 2D art and continued throughout the build to guide and assess along with the agents so they got smarter about what I wanted and what "matched" meant. I always have the AI rate out of 10 and I give it my rating too so it can calibrate. 

I always have codex run full tests on all my code (both games and non-games) as I find it is a better tester than claudecode. It finds bugs that claude just can't see. I also make it playtest the screens with playwright. It is pretty good. Now the full end to end test takes it 95 minutes (it even plays all the platformer levels)  
  
Some stats - I figure this is a 20-30 hour game when you do everything (but I have played it so much I am dizzy). You start in a little seaside village but then you visit 7 other places and have 18 mini platformer levels that break up the 3D, you can meet 19 animal friends each with separate multiple tasks. You have a few collectables like fish and butterflies. And there is even a mail system. It takes 13,000 lines of javascript with three.js. It took about 7 days running as a goal and 7B tokens to get 90% done and I tweaked it from there. 

It took about a month. The first commit was October 18.

A few things I learned along the way

* Make your own design sheets. Models built from my sheets came out better than ones the AI prompted on its own.
* Meshy shreds trees made of small leaves. Ask for a few big, puffy clumps. Or build procedurally. 
* Never let the AI grade its own work or give it strict guidelines. 
* Play it yourself. The checks passed while Pip walked the wrong way once (it was a bug I caused!) 
* Don't forget to learn from others (thank you Mark) who have come before you.

replies.author: jbradleybush
replies.body:
Description from the Itch page: 

Maplebrook is a little seaside village, and it could use a good dog. You are its newest corgi: short legs, big bark. Settle in and make friends. Then go see what is past the edge of the map.

It plays in a desktop browser, with a keyboard and mouse or a gamepad. It isn't made for phones or tablets. Your progress saves in your browser.

**A village full of neighbors**

* 19 animal neighbors to meet, each with their own home and their own errands.
* 53 errands to run for them, like herding ducklings into the pond and carrying letters between villages.
* Small favors every day once you are friends, paid in paw coins, hearts and furniture.
* Five hearts of friendship with every neighbor.
* Letters in your mailbox most mornings, some with a gift tucked inside.

**Eight places to explore**

* Maplebrook village, then Sunpetal Meadows, Mushroom Hollow, Seashell Cove, Frostberry Peaks, Amberleaf Ruins, Starlight Marsh and Sunfish Isle, the last one reached by sailboat.
* 18 side-on caves to run and jump through, each with 3 secret chests to find (54 in all).
* 19 kinds of foe, 10 of them big ones. No fighting with teeth: you bark, you stomp, you get behind them.

**Collect everything**

* 15 fish for the aquarium, 20 butterflies for the Butterfly House and 90 hidden treasures.
* A two-story cottage to furnish, garden decor to place anywhere in the village, and seeds that bloom.
* Five coats, 10 things to wear, 6 poses and a photo mode.

**Take it slow**

* Days and nights pass on their own, with rain showers that make the fish bite.
* Six pastimes that level up as you play.
* The Star Festival, when every friend you have made gathers in the square.

replies.author: jbradleybush
replies.body:
Well, I hope there are a few new twists. 

But if you like Stardew Valley or animal Crossing, you probably will like corgi town

comments.author: Recoil42
comments.body:
Not my type of game, but the art style is super cute, OP.

My only recommendation would be to work on the camera. It got stuck a bunch when I was just walking around. I think it tries to avoid getting caught under overhangs but this causes it to dolly in and get stuck there.
